Malaysia's Chemicals Industry Posts Stable Growth in First Half of 2024

Malaysia’s chemicals sector reported steady trade performance for the first half of 2024, with both exports and imports showing marginal year-on-year increases, according to data released on Tuesday by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).

Total exports of chemicals and chemical products reached RM 50.3 billion from January to June, up 2.1% compared to the same period last year. Imports also rose, registering RM 39.8 billion, a modest 1.7% increase. The steady trade figures reflect ongoing demand from regional partners and the stable performance of domestic manufacturing.

Tan Mei Lin, spokesperson for the Malaysian Chemicals Council, commented, “The sector continues to play a vital role in Malaysia’s export mix, and these figures highlight the resilience of our industry amid global uncertainties. We’re seeing consistent demand from key markets like Singapore, China, and Indonesia.”

Industry analysts noted that the growth was partly driven by increased shipments of specialty chemicals and fertilizers, while demand for base chemicals such as methanol remained consistent. “The chemicals trade is a reliable indicator of industrial activity,” said Dr. Syed Faizal, an economist at Southeast Asia Trade Monitor. “The numbers suggest that Malaysia’s manufacturing sector remains on a solid footing.”

Local companies such as Pacifica Chemie Sdn Bhd and GreenPetra Industries reported steady order books, with no significant disruptions in supply chains or production. The Malaysian Chemicals and Allied Workers Union also confirmed there were no major changes in employment levels across the sector.

MITI officials expect the sector to maintain its momentum in the second half of the year, supported by stable regional demand and ongoing investment in capacity expansion.
